source.title: From Oragnized Shelves to Layered Catalogs: Architectural Explorations for Sparse Autoencoders -- Crosscoders & Ladder SAEs Towards Hierarchical Data Structure

record.tranche_reason: The post discusses hierarchical SAE features, but its reported experiments evaluate graph-regularized crosscoder reconstruction, sparsity, and recovery of an external sentence graph—not feature splitting as dictionary size grows or the claim versions' specified outcomes.
record.gate_note: The reported crosscoder neighborhood-recovery metrics are related to feature geometry but do not measure SAE size-dependent splitting, nested feature families, or the other claim versions. Recorded those metrics under fits_no_version. Reconstruction and sparsity metrics concern crosscoder performance rather than the claim. Ladder SAE results are pending.
record.test_reason: The post proposes hierarchical SAE architectures (graph-regularized crosscoders, Ladder SAEs). Its only results are crosscoder reconstruction, sparsity and recovery of an external E5 sentence graph on GPT-2/TinyStories. It reports no dictionary-size sweep, no split or nested feature families, no absorption measurement, and no comparison of SAE objectives' effect on splitting. Ladder SAE results are pending. It does not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is accurate, with one addition. The authors also claim the graph penalty can substitute for L1 to give sparse, high-fidelity latents (R² 0.935 vs 0.940; 84.7% dead). They say it 'demonstrably aligns latent geometry' with the sentence graph, though the differences are small and mixed. Ladder SAEs are proposed only, with experiments pending.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments train graph-regularized crosscoders for cross-layer alignment; they do not perform the dictionary-size comparison or feature-splitting measurements in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: For crosscoder sentence-graph recovery, Graph has slightly higher Precision@64 than Vanilla, parity at @128, and slightly lower Precision@256; Vanilla has marginally higher NDCG at all reported k values.

fits_no_version.finding: On GPT-2/TinyStories, the graph-regularized crosscoder nearly matches Vanilla on sentence-graph neighborhood recovery. Precision@64 is 0.01340 vs 0.01289, with parity at @128, slightly lower at @256, and marginally lower NDCG at every k. No uncertainty is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A Laplacian/graph penalty on crosscoder latents can align latent geometry with an external semantic neighborhood graph while keeping reconstruction fidelity.

record.problems: The reported experiments do not measure feature splitting or hierarchy directly. The crosscoder neighborhood evaluation uses an external sentence graph and reports no uncertainty estimates; Ladder SAE experiments are pending.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted reconstruction, sparsity, and training-curve results in Sections 4.1.1–4.1.2 because they report crosscoder performance rather than a result on the claim's feature-splitting behavior. No Ladder SAE results were reported.

untested.parts: No dictionary-size variation or coarse-to-fine feature measurement.
No splitting analysis in large models or open SAE releases; only a GPT-2 crosscoder.
Nested feature families are motivated and planned for Ladder SAEs (per-level heatmaps, cross-level correspondence), but no results are reported.
Absorption is mentioned only as a failure mode to stress-test; it is not measured.
No comparison between latents of SAEs of different sizes.
Alternative objectives (graph penalty, isotropic KL) are trained, but their effect on splitting is never measured.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong work-in-progress post with no uncertainty estimates, so the small metric differences cannot be judged. Its relevance to feature splitting is only motivational: hierarchical concepts, coarse/fine granularity, and absorption mentioned as a concern.

versions.untested_parts: No dictionary-size sweep or measurement of coarse-feature input partitioning and nearby directions.
No splitting test across large models or open SAE releases.
No measurement of nested, geometrically close split-feature families mirroring concept hierarchies.
No test of parent-child absorption or whether SAE size or sparsity changes it.
No comparison of larger- and smaller-SAE latents or test for novel latents.
No test of whether the SAE objective produces splitting or whether Matryoshka SAEs change it.

rows.subject: GPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Measured NDCG@64 for latent geometry against sentence-graph neighborhoods.
rows.note: This measures recovery of an external sentence graph, not feature splitting or hierarchical feature families.
rows.check: Rows correctly unlinked. They compare the study's own graph-regularized crosscoder against a Vanilla crosscoder on recovery of an external sentence graph, which is method performance rather than feature splitting. Precision values are as tabulated. They are kept only as fits_no_version context.
